claims.value: Jourdan gives side A scarcely 20,000 combatants in the fourth corps and reserve after losses and hospital admissions.
claims.rationale: Available combined force, not the first assault subset before reserve/king arrival. English rendering (ours): "The king’s army (fourth corps and reserve), reduced by losses and hospital admissions, numbered scarcely 20,000 combatants."

claims.value: Jourdan estimates side B’s assembled army on the evening of 10 August at about 30,000, including 3,000–4,000 cavalry.
claims.rationale: French opponent estimate of previous-evening assembly, not own Spanish muster. English rendering (ours): "It comprised five infantry divisions and three to four thousand cavalry (about thirty thousand men)."

claims.value: Jourdan says Sebastiani engaged before Joseph arrived; Toreno likewise places the initial attack before arrival of the reserve.
claims.rationale: Joseph’s superior role and later presence do not establish his direction of the opening attack. English rendering (ours): "Sebastiani did not think he should wait for him before engaging; he began attacking before his reserve arrived."

claims.rationale: Planned future action is not the observed 11 August posture. English rendering (ours): "They agreed to attack the French on the 12th and rest the troops on the 11th."
